audit.title: Data Streams Architecture
audit.summary: This is a well-structured conceptual overview of Chainlink Data Streams' pull-based architecture, its two implementation modes, and its active-active deployment. Its biggest strength is clean, answer-first section leads and sensible chunk boundaries (14 sections, median 100 words, zero level skips). Its biggest opportunities are missing machine-readable metadata (no JSON-LD, canonical, or dates in the served HTML) and a shortage of concrete numbers — the page leans on vague quantifiers ("low latency," "robust," "sub-second") where hard figures would lift both citability and credibility. Honest verdict: solid, retrievable prose held back by thin specifics and absent structured metadata.

recommendations.title: Add a Standard API vs Streams Trade comparison table
recommendations.where: After the intro list of "two implementation approaches."
recommendations.issue: The two modes are compared only in parallel prose; 0 tables on page.
recommendations.change: Add a table with rows like Retrieval model (pull/REST+WS vs Automation-triggered), Frontrunning mitigation, Gas cost timing, Best-for use case, drawn directly from the two "Key benefits" lists.
recommendations.why: Engines extract *reasons* and build justified "which should I use" answers from tables far more reliably than from separated bullet lists.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/decision-phrased headings
recommendations.where: Section titles and a new short FAQ near the end.
recommendations.issue: Concept-titled sections ("Streams Trade Architecture") miss "how do I choose" and error-phrased queries.
recommendations.change: Add H3s or FAQ entries phrased as questions: "Which Data Streams implementation should I use?", "What do I do when a REST request returns 5xx?", "How do I avoid report gaps during failover?" — answers already exist in body text.
recommendations.why: Headings matching the exact question devs type win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses even when the answer is present verbatim.

recommendations.title: Add `TechArticle` JSON-LD, canonical URL, and visible last-updated
recommendations.issue: Measured — 0 JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, dateModified absent.
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` schema with `headline`, `dateModified`, `inLanguage`, and a self-referential canonical; surface a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and freshness signals raise agent parseability and trust; likely a site-template fix (see off-page note).

recommendations.title: Replace vague quantifiers with concrete figures
recommendations.where: Intro ("low-latency"), Standard API benefits ("sub-second data latency"), Aggregation Network description.
recommendations.issue: Measured vague quantifiers "many, various, low latency, robust"; 0 numerals with units.
recommendations.change: State actual figures where public — e.g. report cadence/latency in milliseconds, number of isolated origins/data centers, WebSocket subscription limit ("up to two" is already good — extend that pattern).
recommendations.why: Quantitative claims are among the highest-lift changes for citation rate; qualitative-only prose underperforms.

recommendations.title: Add a minimal StreamsLookup / verify code sketch
recommendations.where: "Example trading flow using Streams Trade," step 4 and step 7.
recommendations.issue: Identifiers `StreamsLookup`, `checkCallback`, `verify` named but no snippet; 0 fenced blocks.
recommendations.change: Add a short Solidity fence showing the `revert StreamsLookup(...)` signature and the `verify` call, tagged `solidity`, linking to the full guide.
recommendations.why: Agents completing integration tasks lift copy-pasteable signatures; a labeled snippet anchors the canonical API against generic priors.

recommendations.title: Name the tempting-wrong retry pattern as a Don't
recommendations.issue: Good guidance, but "Do not retry on 4xx" is the only explicit Don't.
recommendations.change: Add an explicit Don't for the common mistake — e.g. "Don't retry without exponential backoff and jitter; naive fixed-interval retries amplify load during a site failover."
recommendations.why: Naming the common-but-wrong pattern defends against models answering from generic retry priors.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifiers: "low latency," "robust fault tolerance," "various array of events" — replace with specifics where possible.
Missing dates/schema: no visible freshness signal or structured metadata (stale-risk to engines).
No walls of prose, no broken cross-references, no keyword stuffing detected.
offPageNotes: JSON-LD, canonical, and og/twitter tags are almost certainly template-level — fix once in the docs layout to benefit all Data Streams pages, not just this one.
The page already references `/llms.txt`; ensure this URL is listed there so the canonical-hub retrieval path is complete.
CLI note: raw `<head>` was not captured — pass it for a definitive metadata read before acting on the schema findings.
